notes: §1985:IV.5.3.1 prints a source program as identification-division, then [ environment-division ], [ data-division ], [ procedure-division ] and [ end-program-header ], each bracket optional and in that order (§1985:IV.5.2: the divisions "are grouped into four divisions which are sequenced in the following order"). The grammar rule programUnit is that format (identificationDivision, then environmentDivision?, dataDivision?, procedureDivision?, endProgramHeader?), so a division out of order or written twice has no parse; the one 1985 difference from 2023, the required identification division header, is the edition gate VisitIdentificationDivision (COBOL0900 at 85 for a unit that opens at PROGRAM-ID), and SourceUnitShape.Screen checks the end marker's keyword. Probed at --std 85: an identification division alone, with an empty environment and data division, and with END PROGRAM compile; DATA before ENVIRONMENT, DATA after PROCEDURE, two DATA or ENVIRONMENT divisions, two end program headers and a program with no identification division are refused. The witness runs the identification and procedure divisions alone. LEAD outside this row (§1985:X.2.3.1 prints [ procedure-division ] and [ source-program ] ... as separate brackets): SourceUnitShape.Screen applies the 2023 format at every edition and refuses at 85 a program that contains a program and has no procedure division (COBOL2274, probe n1.cob); no kb/Work note names it.

next.reason: 1985 program structure is identification-division [environment-division] [data-division] [procedure-division] [end-program-header], and the identification-division opens with the required IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. header (IV.6.1.3.1). §2023:10.6.1 program-definition keeps the division order and the optional END PROGRAM marker but writes "[ IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. ]" and adds [ options-paragraph ]; §2023:11.2.1 restates the bracketed header for the identification division. A program that starts at PROGRAM-ID, refused by 1985, is accepted. End-marker presence rules belong to 1985 VI.2.3.3 GR2 and X.2.3.2 SR1, not to this format. Compile-time only.
